Any citizen of India can file an RTI application.
RTI application fee for central public authorities is Rs 10.
RTI application fee for Maharashtra state authorities is Rs 10.
Applicants below poverty line (BPL) are exempt from all RTI fees.
The PIO must reply to an RTI application within 30 days of receipt.
If the information concerns life or liberty of a person, the PIO must reply within 48 hours.
If the application is submitted through an APIO, 5 extra days are added to the reply deadline.
If the application is sent to the wrong PIO, it must be transferred within 5 days and the applicant informed.
Cost for providing information is Rs 2 per page for central public authorities.
Cost for providing information is Rs 2 per page for Maharashtra state authorities.
First appeal must be filed within 30 days of the PIO reply (or non-reply) to the first appellate authority.
Fee for filing a first appeal in Maharashtra is Rs 20.
Second appeal lies with the Central Information Commission (CIC) or State Information Commission (SIC) within 90 days of first appeal order.
Certain information is exempt from disclosure, including national security, cabinet papers, personal privacy and information given in fiduciary capacity.
RTI applications to central ministries can be filed online at the RTI Online Portal.
RTI applications to Maharashtra state departments can be filed online at the Aaple Sarkar RTI portal.
RTI applications in Maharashtra must not exceed 150 words for the information sought.
Every public authority must designate a Public Information Officer (PIO) to receive and reply to RTI applications.
Public authorities with sub-offices must designate an Assistant Public Information Officer (APIO) at each sub-office.
An RTI application may be written in Hindi, English or the official language of the area.
